# What’s new with Medicare? 5 ways Medicare is changing for 2027


*By[Whitney Stidom](https://news.ehealthinsurance.com/experts/whitney-stidom) , vice president of consumer enablement, **[eHealth](https://www.ehealthinsurance.com/)***


Every fall,


about


**[70 million Americans](https://data.cms.gov/summary-statistics-on-beneficiary-enrollment/medicare-and-medicaid-reports/medicare-monthly-enrollment)** — or about 20% of the population —


can


compare their Medicare options and make changes.


Whether


that’s


picking a new Medicare


Advantage


plan or


a Part D prescription drug plan


, the Annual Enrollment Period (Oct. 15 through Dec. 7) is a


crucial


seven-week window


that will affect the health and finances of


beneficiaries during 2027


.


But every year Medicare


p


lans


can


change


in ways


that beneficiaries and their families should be aware of.


Here are five of the most


important changes


for


next year


:


**Improved coverage for GLP-1 drugs.** While Medicare


plans


ha


ve


long covered GLP-1 drugs to treat chronic conditions such as diabetes, access to these medications for obesity has been limited. That is starting to change


, both through Medicare Advantage plans and the


new


**[Medicare G LP-1 Bridge program](https://www.cms.gov/medicare/coverage/prescription-drug-coverage/medicare-glp-1-bridge/information-providers)** .


For instance


,


most


Medicare Advantage plans (93%) will cover at least one GLP-1 drug to treat obesity


for eligible beneficiaries


in 2027, up from just 5% of plans


in 2026


, according to


eHealth data


.


**Higher Medicare Part D costs .** About


**[56 million Americans](https://www.kff.org/medicare/analyzing-changes-in-medicare-part-d-enrollment-for-2026/)**


are enrolled in


Medicare Part D


coverage


, either


through Medicare Advantage or a stand-alone plan. Many


of them will pay more out of pocket


for this coverage


,


including


in terms of


monthly


premiums


, deductibles


,


and


out-of-pocket maximums


.


With


a temporary federal program


that


had


supported lower Part D premiums ending


this year, Medicare


beneficiaries can expect to pay more out of pocket for their prescription medications


in 2027


.


**Medicare Advantage plan closures and changes** **.**


As


in recent years


, many Medicare Advantage plans are being cancelled or


changing


for 2027


. Over


**[3 million Americans](https://247wallst.com/health-and-healthcare/2026/10/19/3-2-million-seniors-will-lose-their-medicare-advantage-plans-in-2027-and-their-replacement-options-are-shrinking/)** are enrolled in Medicare Advantage plans that have been cancelled for 2027, while millions more are currently in plans that will have


updates


related


to costs, provider networks, or benefits like dental, vision, and hearing.


To


determine


if this


impacts


you,


review your


Annual Notice of Change (ANOC) letter


, which


you should have received in the mail and


is


available via


your plan's website or app.


**Enrollment caps for some Medicare Advantage plans.** Amid these chan


g


e


s


and closures,


more health insurance companies are capping enrollment in certain plans. That means once a certain number of


Medicare beneficiaries enroll in a Medicare Advantage plan, the insurer may stop accepting applications


if the membership capacity has been reached


.


The takeaway


: If you find a


Medicare Advantage


plan you like,


act soon or you may miss the opportunity to enroll


.


**Continued access to telehealth services.** **** Many Medicare beneficiaries first tapped into telehealth services during the COVID-19 pandemic, with access granted through a temporary program authorized by Congress. That access has been extended once again, ensuring virtual care


remains


accessible and reimbursable for Medicare beneficiaries through at least the end of 2027.


Most


**[Medicare beneficiaries (71%)](https://news.ehealthinsurance.com/news/survey-half-of-medicare-beneficiaries-have-skipped-medical-care-in-the-past-year-due-to-confusion-over-their-coverage)** say shopping for a new plan is confusing


,


which is understandable given the annual changes


. But


by


taking the time to compare your options


and understand how Medicare plans may be changing


for 2027


, you can


make


a more


informed decision based on your personal needs


.


-


***[Whitney Stidom](https://news.ehealthinsurance.com/experts/whitney-stidom)** is vice president of consumer enablement at **[eHealth](http://www.ehealthinsurance.com/)** , an online health insurance marketplace that helps consumers navigate their health benefit decisions .*
